cli.help.code_index.search.fixed_strings: Match *pattern* as a literal substring, not a regex (like grep -F).

cli.help.code_index.search.max_count: Stop after N matches (like grep -m). Default: no limit.
cli.help.code_index.search.pattern: Pattern to match against each item's rendered line. A Python regex by default (feels like `grep -E`), case-sensitive; use -F for a literal substring.
cli.help.code_index.show.desc: Print one file's full function/method detail from the code-index.
cli.help.code_index.show.path: Project-relative path of the file (or directory) to detail.
cli.help.daemon.app: Resident control-plane daemon (supervises local flows, dials the server)
cli.help.daemon.start.daemon_key: Secret daemon credential sent to the central server so it can bind this machine to its owner. When omitted, the SE3_DAEMON_KEY environment variable is used. The key is held only in memory and is never written to logs or the daemon status file. Prefer the environment variable so the secret does not land in shell history.
cli.help.daemon.start.foreground: Run the daemon in the foreground (do not detach)
cli.help.daemon.start.server_url: Central server URL the daemon dials out to. An explicit port (wss://host:9000) is always preserved; when the port is omitted it is completed per the scheme — wss:// (and https://) default to 443, ws:// (and http://) default to 8080 (the tianluo-server plaintext default). So a bare wss://host dials :443, not :8080.
cli.help.daemon.status.desc: Show the tianluo daemon's running state and tracked flows.
cli.help.end_session.desc: End and archive a session (worktree is cleaned up; uncommitted work is NOT merged).
cli.help.end_session.flow_id: Flow id to end (default: the main project's active session).
cli.help.end_session.no_archive_worktree: Terminate the process but leave the worktree in place (do not archive).
cli.help.end_session.pid: Hint: pid of the live luo run process to terminate.

cli.help.merge_unlock.force: Force-release a lock whose holder process is still alive. This may break merge mutual exclusion — use only when you are certain no active merge is running. A stale lock is cleaned up without this flag.
cli.help.migrate.app: Run a registered version/format migration (list / run <id>).
cli.help.migrate.run.migrator_id: ID of the migration to run (see `luo migrate list`)
cli.help.migrate.run.no_delete_specs: Keep tianluo/specs/ in place (salvage + build only; for inspection).
cli.help.run.desc: tianluo Run — Unified entry point for the flow engine.
cli.help.run.discover: Discovery mode - explore requirements with user before analyzing
cli.help.run.from_issue: Run flow from an existing issue (ID or interactive selection). Combine with --discover to start the issue-sourced flow from the discovery step.
cli.help.run.output_format: Output sink: 'cli' (Rich rendering, default) or 'json' (structured NDJSON event stream)
cli.help.run.preset: Run a preset prompt task by name (mutually exclusive with --type; the preset carries its own type). Use '--preset list' to list available presets.

cli.help.run.worktree: Isolation mode: run the flow in a dedicated git worktree (concurrent with other --worktree runs), then auto-merge the result back into the current branch. Without this flag, the flow runs in place (synchronous mode).
cli.help.salvage.desc: Salvage work from an abnormally terminated session.
cli.help.worktree.gc.dry_run: Report what WOULD be reclaimed without touching disk or branches.
cli.help.worktree.gc.max_age_hours: Only reclaim terminal worktree runs whose engine.json has been idle at least this long (default: 24). Guards a just-completed run still awaiting a human merge.

e2e.probe.not_installed: Container runtime '{runtime}' is not installed, or is not on PATH.
e2e.probe.timeout: '{runtime} info' did not answer within {timeout}s; the runtime looks unavailable.
e2e.probe.none_available: No usable container runtime found. e2e needs docker or podman runnable by the current user. Tried — {tried}
e2e.probe.explicit_unavailable: The configured e2e runtime '{runtime}' is unavailable: {detail} tianluo does not silently fall back to the other runtime, because switching would change the image cache, storage location and UID mapping behind your back.
e2e.probe.remediation:
How to fix (tianluo never escalates privileges — e2e only requires that you can run 'docker info' or 'podman info' as your normal user):
  1. Docker: have an administrator add your user to the 'docker' group, then log out and back in so the new group takes effect.
  2. Podman: install podman — it is rootless natively and works out of the box for an unprivileged user.
  3. Rootless Docker: run the 'dockerd-rootless-setuptool.sh install' script shipped with Docker to set up a per-user daemon.
e2e.error.dependency_missing: The e2e feature requires the '{dependency}' package, which is not installed.
e2e.error.dependency_missing_for: e2e {feature} requires the '{dependency}' package, which is not installed.
e2e.remediation.install_extra:
Install the e2e extra:
    pip install '{extra}'
e2e.schema.invalid_choice: {value} is not valid here; expected one of: {choices}.
e2e.schema.invalid_threshold: threshold must be a number between 0 and 1 (got {value}).
e2e.schema.required_one_of: needs at least one of: {fields} — required for {context}.
e2e.schema.no_services: declares no service; an e2e environment needs at least one container.
e2e.schema.no_assertions: declares no assertion; a scenario that asserts nothing verifies nothing.
e2e.schema.invalid_service_name: '{name}' cannot be used as a container/DNS name; use lowercase letters, digits and '-', starting and ending with an alphanumeric, at most 63 characters.
e2e.schema.duplicate_service: service name '{name}' is declared more than once; names must be unique because each one is also the service's hostname on the shared network.
e2e.schema.duplicate_scenario: scenario name '{name}' is already used by {other}; names must be unique because e2e.scenarios selects by name.
e2e.schema.unknown_driver: names service '{driver}', which is not declared in {environment}.
e2e.schema.baseline_missing: references baseline '{baseline}', which is not present under {directory}.
e2e.schema.ladder_visual_regression_unde: compares against a baseline screenshot (assertion tier 2) without declaring 'visual_regression: true'. Tier 2 is opt-in and is allowed only when the subject under test genuinely is a visual rendering.
e2e.schema.ladder_semantic_visual_undecl: asks an LLM to look at an image (assertion tier 3) without declaring 'semantic_visual: true'. Tier 3 is the last resort and must be stated explicitly.
e2e.schema.ladder_evidence_required: is a tier-3 semantic visual assertion but does not set 'require_evidence: true'. An LLM verdict is only admissible together with a reviewable description of the evidence.
e2e.schema.ladder_flag_on_deterministic: sets '{flag}' on '{kind}', which is a deterministic assertion. Tier flags belong only on the higher-tier assertion they unlock.
e2e.schema.ladder_downgrade_available: escalates to '{kind}' while also providing '{field}', which a deterministic tier-1 assertion can check directly. Use the lowest tier that can express the check.
e2e.schema.ladder_visual_driving_undecla: drives the UI by screen coordinates without the scenario declaring 'visual_driving: true'. Coordinate driving is reserved for GUIs that offer no programmatic entry point.
e2e.schema.ladder_driving_downgrade_avai: clicks at screen coordinates while also naming a selector; drive the interaction through the selector instead.
